events.title: Tailwind CSS 1.0 released
events.summary: Adam Wathan released [Tailwind] [CSS] 1.0 on May 13, 2019 — the first stable version of the utility-first [CSS] framework.
events.about: [Tailwind] 1.0 (`flex`, `pt-4`, `text-lg`) let developers style UIs by composing utility classes instead of writing custom [CSS] — paired with PurgeCSS for production bundles. It challenged Bootstrap's component model and became the default stack with [React], Next.js, and Laravel.

narrative.whyChosen: [Tailwind] 1.0 validated utility-first [CSS] as a mainstream styling approach.
narrative.whyImportant: Composable utilities replaced hand-written stylesheets for thousands of design systems.
narrative.problemSolved: Naming [CSS] classes and fighting specificity wars slowed front-end iteration.

events.title: Shopware 6 developer preview released
events.summary: [Shopware] unveiled [Shopware] 6 at the [Shopware] Community Day on May 23, 2019 — a complete rewrite on [Symfony] 4, Vue.js admin, and a 100% [API]-first architecture.
events.about: [Shopware] 6 split storefront, administration, and core into headless services — Twig and Bootstrap 4 for the default storefront, [REST] APIs for every function. The developer preview let the community test the platform before [Shopware] 6.1 stable in January 2020.

narrative.whyChosen: [Shopware] 6 preview signaled Europe's leading OSS commerce platform going headless.
narrative.whyImportant: [API]-first architecture aligned [Shopware] with composable commerce trends.
narrative.problemSolved: [Shopware] 5's monolith could not support omnichannel and headless storefront demands.
